title: Diffusion Safety-Lane Controller for Staged Upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: ship a staged-rollout controller ("Diffusion Safety-Lane Controller") that implements lane-based progressive delivery for Redwood releases with explicit LTS fencing. The controller should: 1) orchestrate lane promotions (shadow -> alpha -> beta -> stable) with configurable traffic percentages and hold windows; 2) evaluate multi-signal health policies (P99 latency, error-rate, token-cost divergence, output-regression-failed-evals) to automatically pause or roll back promotions; 3) ensure LTS channel isolation by fencing LTS traffic to builds labeled as LTS or LTS-compatible; 4) integrate with feature flags and the console rollout UI so PMs can start/stop promotions and audit gate decisions; 5) provide a lightweight rollout-simulator to run what-if traffic curves against historical telemetry; 6) emit structured events to the rollout audit stream for compliance and postmortem.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller can declare and execute four lanes with target traffic allocations: shadow(0%), alpha(1%), beta(5%), stable(100% over time); 2) Promotion halts automatically when any configured SLO triggers: 99th latency > 750ms or error-rate increase > 0.5 percentage points for 5m rolling window or eval regression > 2% on golden prompts; 3) Operator can manually override or force-promote via Console and CLI and the action is recorded in audit logs; 4) LTS traffic routed only to releases with tag 'lts-v*' and controller prevents mixing LTS with non-LTS variants; 5) Simulator produces a promotion-plan report and shows expected cost delta and estimated tail latency impact; 6) End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (region outage, spike in requests) executed and documented in QA runbook.
implementation_notes: Architecture: controller runs as a control-plane service that talks to the routing layer (RTG) and the fleet manager. Single source of truth is a rollout resource referencing release artifacts (image id, model hash, quantization profile) and lane policy. Policy DSL: JSON schema with 'lane', 'traffic_pct', 'hold_minutes', 'gate_signals' (list), 'rollback_policy' (scoring thresholds). Health signals: integrate telemetry extractor service (trace/metrics/logs) and the evals pipeline (batch evals job). Rollback scorer: weighted combination of SLO violations and regression counts; threshold leads to automatic reversal to previous stable. Safety nets: rate limit promotions, cooldown backoff, and a circuit-breaker that can opt to route to a cheaper compatible variant under capacity pressure. Persistence: rollout state persisted in cluster KV and emitted to audit topic (Kafka).

Implement lane controller core state machine
Integrate with RTG routing API for percentage routing
Create QA runbook and chaos tests
Add e2e tests and canary smoke checks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives in auto-rollback due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require multiple signal agreement, and a confidence multiplier. Risk: LTS traffic misrouted to non-LTS build. Mitigation: denylist mixing via server-side fencing and pre-deployment validation. Risk: rollout controller becomes single point of failure. Mitigation: leader election with hot-standby controllers and read-only fallback mode where routing falls back to existing stable mappings.

notes: Try to keep the rollout policy expressive but brief; avoid creating 20 distinct lane types. Keep default promotion curve conservative: 1% for 30m, 5% for 60m, 25% for 3h, then ramp to 100% over 24h unless manual expedite. Ensure Console exposes 'fast-track' gating for infra emergencies under a special RBAC flag.
